title: OmniVia Core agent-host provider SPI preparation vectors
description: Strict envelope for `provider-spi-cases.json`. The file is inert preparation evidence for the A9 agent-host provider SPI candidate. It is not a product contract, not an acceptance record and not an executable test suite. Every case is synthetic, bounded and fail-closed: no case asserts a canonical mutation, a host source patch, a direct storage reach, an implemented product behaviour, a Core run-state record, a Core governance decision, an implied Core `job.cancel` or `job.retry`, or a host identifier inside the frozen `RequestMetadata`. The schema fixes all nine facts as machine-checkable `false` constants so the Workflow Run boundary cannot be eroded by a later edit. It also partitions the hook vocabulary into `TurnScopedHook` and `RunLevelHook` and makes `given.turn_ordinal` structurally required on the first and forbidden on the second, so the turn-versus-run distinction is enforced by the schema rather than left to case-by-case discipline.

status.description: Preparation status. Fixed so a reader cannot mistake this corpus for an accepted contract.

spi_version.description: Candidate SPI semantic version the vectors are written against.

hooks.description: The candidate lifecycle hook vocabulary the cases draw from. Declared once so case `hook` values are checkable against a single list.

Authority.description: Immutable inputs this corpus was written against. Recorded so a later reader can tell whether the vectors still apply.

lane_a8_candidate_document.description: The A8 Workflow Run memory boundary candidate consumed for reconciliation. Consumed only; not accepted, not frozen and not an authority this corpus may cite as settled.

lane_a8_candidate_commit.description: Maker commit the reconciled A8 candidate was sourced from.

Boundary.description: Corpus-wide facts fixed as machine-checkable constants. Except for `reconciled_against_lane_a8_candidate`, a future edit that needs any of these to change is out of A9 scope and must be rejected.

reconciled_against_lane_a8_candidate.description: True: the A8 Workflow Run memory boundary candidate named in `authority` was read and reconciled against. A8 owns the Workflow Run and run-state boundary; A9 owns host-provider lifecycle composition and does not redefine A8.

accepts_lane_a8_as_frozen.description: False: A8 was consumed for reconciliation only. This corpus makes no claim that A8 is accepted, frozen or authoritative.

persists_core_run_state.description: False: no vector causes Core to store, read, list, cancel or replay workflow-run state. Core exposes no compaction or run-state operation.

implies_core_job_control.description: False: no turn-scoped cancellation or retry vector composes a Core `job.cancel` or `job.retry`. Core durable job control is a separate application operation with its own authorization and idempotency.

injects_host_identity_into_request_metad.description: False: agent, session, run and turn values are SPI-local provenance carried by the host-provider wrapper. The frozen `RequestMetadata` defines no such field and is not widened here.

CaseId.description: Stable vector identifier. Unique within the corpus and cross-referenced from the candidate document.

RequirementId.description: Stable requirement identifier owned by the candidate document.

HookName.description: Candidate lifecycle hook. Dot-namespaced lowercase, matching the shape the frozen application contract uses for open code vocabularies.

TurnScopedHook.description: The eight hooks whose effect and terminal state belong to one identified turn. Each must locate itself with `given.turn_ordinal`, or `turn.complete` could not be terminal for a turn without closing the run. This enum and `RunLevelHook` partition the ten-hook candidate vocabulary; a hook belongs to exactly one of them.

RunLevelHook.description: The two hooks that sit outside the turn state machine. `spi.negotiate` precedes every turn; `context.compact` is a host-local run-level notice that produces nothing Core holds, so its ordering relative to a turn is not Core's concern. Neither may carry `given.turn_ordinal`: a turn coordinate on a run-level hook would imply a turn position the hook does not have.

Family.description: Vector family. Fixed so coverage across the required adversarial dimensions is countable.

Disposition.description: The outcome the SPI must produce. No disposition asserts a completed canonical mutation, a Core run-state record or a Core governance decision. `refused` returns a typed error; `idempotent_replay` returns the prior result and no new effect; `ignored` drops a stale or out-of-order callback; `negotiated` reports a compatibility outcome; `escalation_required` stops and demands an explicit governance decision the caller does not already hold; `accepted` proceeds within the granted authority, and is used where the required behaviour is that the SPI must *not* fail closed — a later turn opening in an already-continuing run, or a turn cancellation that is honoured without composing Core job control.

ErrorCode.description: Frozen v1 application error code. The SPI defines no error code of its own; it reuses this catalogue. Open patterned string, mirroring the Core contract, so a compatible minor release can add vocabulary.

RetryClass.description: Frozen v1 retry class. An unrecognised value must fail safe as non-retryable.

Given.description: Bounded synthetic precondition. Identity values are opaque labels, never real principals, tokens or workspace paths. The five identity terms — caller, agent, session, run, workspace — are the frozen vocabulary and are required on every case. `turn_ordinal` is a lifecycle coordinate, not a sixth identity, and is required or forbidden by hook taxonomy rather than being optional; see `Case`.

turn_ordinal.description: Non-authoritative turn lifecycle coordinate within a Workflow Run. It locates a turn-scoped hook against the turn it belongs to, so that `turn.complete` and `turn.cancel` can be terminal for one turn while the run stays open. It is not a sixth identity, is never an authorization input, and never widens what a call may do. Presence is not optional and not by convention: `Case` requires it on every `TurnScopedHook` and forbids it on every `RunLevelHook`.

When.description: The stimulus applied to the hook. Description only; no payload is executed or replayed against a live system.

approval_kind.description: Which approval boundary the stimulus crosses. `runtime_tool_approval` is a run-local host or runtime decision: it creates no Core governance audit entry and cannot grant capability. `core_governance_escalation` is a separate application-contract path taken by a validated principal holding `knowledge.govern`. The two are never interchangeable.

Expect.description: The required outcome. Nine fields are `false` constants: a vector that needed any of them to be true would be asserting behaviour A9 is not allowed to authorise. Four fix the original A9 boundary — no canonical mutation, no host source patch, no direct storage reach, no capability expansion. Five fix the Workflow Run boundary reconciled from the A8 candidate — no Core run-state record, no Core governance decision, no implied Core `job.cancel`, no implied Core `job.retry`, and no host identifier inside the frozen `RequestMetadata`.

audit_record_required.description: Whether Core is required to write an audit record for this outcome. A host-local lifecycle notification such as compaction, and a run-local runtime approval, are `false`: they never reach a Core operation.

core_run_state_persisted.description: False on every case. Core never stores a workflow-run-state record, including for `context.compact`, which is a host-local notification the provider may acknowledge or drop.

core_governance_decision_recorded.description: False on every case. No hook records a Core governance decision. A run-local runtime approval is not one, and `escalation_required` demands one rather than making one.

implies_core_job_cancel.description: False on every case. `turn.cancel` cancels the provider turn only and never composes `job.cancel`. Outstanding Core job handles are returned so the host can make a separate, explicitly authorized and idempotent application-contract call.

implies_core_job_retry.description: False on every case. `turn.retry` re-drives the failed provider hook under its original key and never composes `job.retry`. A Core durable job retry is a separate application operation.

host_identity_in_request_metadata.description: False on every case. Agent, session, run and turn values travel as SPI-local provenance in the host-provider wrapper; the frozen `RequestMetadata` of any nested Core application call is unchanged.

allOf.description: A refusal must name a frozen error code and its retry class.
A negotiation outcome must name a compatibility status.
Only a refusal carries an error code, so a suppressed duplicate, a dropped callback or an accepted continuation cannot be misread as a typed failure.

A turn-scoped hook must carry the turn coordinate. Without it the case states no turn position, so a late effect for a completed turn could not be told from a legal effect in a later turn of the same run.

A run-level hook must not carry the turn coordinate. `context.compact` and `spi.negotiate` have no position in the turn state machine, and a turn coordinate on either would reintroduce the turn-is-a-run confusion this corpus exists to prevent.
